note: A field-level crosswalk between AVE's evidence-provenance properties and the agent-evidence-vocabulary registry, which names the axes an execution-evidence claim is read on: who observed the execution, how directly, what the claim leaves out, and why a published record's derived value changed. The unit is a schema property rather than a category, because the two sides describe different things: AVE enumerates behavioral vulnerability classes and the registry names the provenance axes any claim about an execution carries. They meet at two places: how AVE says where its evidence came from, and how an AVE record says why one of its own derived values changed. Read coverage before trusting a row: at the AVE commit above, 16 of the 89 records carry at least one of evidence_vantage and verification_basis, and none carries evidence_method. Nine records carry evidence_vantage (eight artifact, one substrate, AVE-2026-00074) and seven carry verification_basis (all artifact_reconstructed); this was checked by reading every record file in the pinned tree rather than by reading the schema. One record, AVE-2026-00074, carries a revisions entry, with reason_code declaration_added. The rows for evidence_vantage, verification_basis and revisions[].reason_code are therefore evidence: emitted, and the rows for evidence_method and evidence_basis_engines stay evidence: inferred, established by comparing two schema definitions. AVE records are unsigned JSON files in a git repository, so emitted here means that a record carries the field and a reviewer can fetch it at the pinned commit, which is the rule this file set on 2026-09-15; the registry's own definition of emitted names a signed statement, and whether a row meets the registry's promotion rule is for the registry to decide. A row moves to emitted when a record carries the field and a reviewer can fetch it.

mappings.notes: Value sets are identical and so is the composition rule: both take the weakest input, so a claim mixing substrate and artifact observations inherits artifact. The two definitions were written independently and reached the same two-value split, which is the case for mapping them exact rather than structural. The registry adds one consumer-side requirement AVE's schema does not state, that a consumer with no policy-pinned substrate root must treat a substrate row as unattested rather than infer the root from the claim. At 0.8.0 the registry term is unchanged in values and composition.

Identical value sets, identical weakest-input composition, and both treat reconstructed as the floor a producer may always truthfully state. AVE's schema says an absent value reads as reconstructed; the registry does not state a default, so a producer emitting both sides should write the value rather than rely on either reading. No record carries the field at the pinned commit, so the row stays inferred.

The four values are the product of the two axes above, which is what scripts/write_verification_basis.py composes. The registry keeps the axes separate and does not define the composed term, so this is a structural correspondence rather than a term pairing: a consumer holding an AVE verification_basis can split it into the two registry axes without loss, and a consumer holding both registry values can compose the AVE value without loss. Seven records carry a declared value, all artifact_reconstructed, and validate_records.py checks each against the derivation, so the declaration is falsifiable.

One value carries vantage information and the rest do not. external_authority means a party outside the observed artifact answered, which is the substrate side of the registry's axis; sandbox observes execution and is the other candidate. pattern, yara, semgrep, llm and magika all read the artifact's own bytes, so they sit on the artifact side. AVE's own schema already composes this field into verification_basis by weakest input, so the partial mapping is not a gap in AVE, it is the reason the composed field exists.

Same four codes, same meaning, same entry shape: date, field, from, to and reason_code required, reason optional, append-only, and a record with no revisions array makes no claim about its own history. AVE copied the codes from the registry when it added the array (#360) and states that its enum stands on its own and does not follow later changes there; the four codes were compared with revision_reason at 0.8.0 and are identical. One record carries an entry, AVE-2026-00074, with reason_code declaration_added for evidence_vantage (null to substrate); the other three codes are valid in the schema and no record uses them. AVE adds checks the registry does not state, such as date order and an unbroken from-to chain per field, which are validator behavior and do not change the correspondence.

gaps.reason: Declares which identity's signature backs which field inside one mixed claim. AVE records a vulnerability class rather than a signed claim, so there is no per-field signer to partition.

Distinguishes a timestamp anchored to a beacon from one the producer asserts. AVE records carry published and last_updated as editorial dates on the record, not as claims about when an execution was observed.
Describes the network posture an execution ran under. AVE classifies component behavior independently of any one run's containment.
States the population a claim was measured over. An AVE record is a class definition rather than a measurement, so it has no denominator to declare.
Carries, inside the signed bytes, what a claim deliberately leaves out. AVE has no signed-claim envelope for this to sit in; the nearest thing is prose in vulnerability_rationale.

A recomputable outcome lattice over one execution: fail, degraded, pass_indirect, pass. AVE scores a class with AIVSS rather than recording an outcome, and the registry's own out-of-scope block rules out reading its lattice as a threshold anyway.

Names whether the witness is the observed party, a peer or an outside party. An AVE record is a class definition with no witness, so there is nothing for the field to describe; evidence_vantage says what was observed, which the registry keeps orthogonal to this.
Says whether the latest time a record existed is proven by an external anchor. AVE records carry editorial published and last_updated dates and no anchor.
The companion of commitment_anchor, which AVE has no counterpart for.
Says whether a platform re-derived the signed subject or signed what the caller supplied. AVE records are not platform attestations.
Says whether the intent an action ran under was committed before the action. An AVE record describes a behavior class, not an action taken under an intent.

Says which party produced the evidence a record is assembled from. AVE records name a researcher and sources, but no field states whether the producer was the runtime itself, a control plane or a log import.
Says whether a guarantee was shown by sources independent of the party it is about. AVE records make no guarantee about a named party.
Names the role a party holds with respect to one evidence set. AVE records have no audited provider, auditing organisation or evaluating authority.
A structured statement of who can direct the party a claim is about. AVE classifies component behavior and says nothing about ownership or control.

Says which kind of act produced an evidence item: a document read, a system queried, a person asked, a test performed. AVE's evidence_kind_default names a scanner's detection technique, which is a different question.
Says whether a claim is about a tool, an agent or an organization. An AVE record is about a behavioral class of a component, which is none of the three.
Says how the before-state root of an observed interval was obtained. AVE records observe no interval.
Says whether the evidence set a claim rests on was sufficient. AVE carries a confidence prior and a mutation count, neither of which assesses a set.
Names the event that ends a standing claim and obliges a re-assessment. AVE records are revised through the revisions array, which records what changed and not what would invalidate the record.
The outcome of one decision on a proposed change to an agent harness. AVE records make no admission decision.
The closed names of the checks an admission rests on. AVE has no admission.
How an evaluation result attached to an admission was obtained. AVE has no admission.
Says whether a guard's replay checked every trace in its snapshot. AVE records do not replay traces.
The SHA-256 that freezes the recorded traces a guard was replayed over. AVE records do not replay traces.
Says whether a candidate harness grants authority its parent lacked. AVE records classify behavior and do not compare a candidate with a parent.
The definition of done for one task, sealed before the agent's first turn. AVE has no task.
The record of one done decision. AVE records no decision about a run.
Whether acceptance commands pass on the agent's final tree. AVE has no acceptance commands.
A path the contract places off limits to the agent. AVE has no contract.
A command the agent says it ran, parsed from its transcript. AVE records hold no transcript.
The exec events an independent observer recorded for a command. AVE records hold no run.
The action a published policy table returns for a run's verdict history. AVE has no run history.
The verdict that the records neither show a claim true nor false. AVE records a class definition, which has no such verdict.
A scanner's prior on a single-engine match. The registry's out-of-scope block excludes scored assessment, so there is deliberately no term for it and there will not be one.
Says when in a component's lifecycle a class is detectable. The registry has no lifecycle axis.
Says which layer of a component a detector reads. The registry's vantage axis is about the relation between observer and observed, not about which layer was read, and the two are orthogonal.
A scanner hint naming the detection technique. The registry names where a claim came from rather than how it was computed.

Free text describing the detection approach (static scan, semantic analysis, behavioral sandbox, network monitoring). The registry names where a claim came from and has no term for how a scanner worked.

coverage.what_the_counts_leave_out: registry_terms_mapped counts observation_vantage, observation_directness and revision_reason, and registry_terms_unmapped plus those three is 37. verification_basis covers the same two axes composed, so it is counted once as structural rather than twice. ave_evidence_fields_total counts the ten schema properties this file maps or lists as gaps: the five mapped (evidence_vantage, evidence_method, verification_basis, evidence_basis_engines, revisions) and the five in gaps. ave_records_carrying_any_mapped_field is 16, the union of the nine records carrying evidence_vantage and the seven carrying verification_basis, and it does not count the one record carrying revisions or the 89 carrying evidence_basis_engines, which is the partial row. Every figure was read from the record files at the pinned commit.

revision_note: 2026-10-27 refresh of the 2026-09-15 revision. Source: AVE record_count 80 to 89 and the pinned commit moved to 4032785b. Target: retargeted from agent-evidence-vocabulary 0.2.0 (8 terms, commit 66177d65, now in the archived probityai-archive/agent-evidence-vocabulary) to 0.8.0 (37 terms) in probityai/agent-evidence under packages/vocabulary, read at commit 5fe04d8f; the 0.2.0 values are kept under previous on both endpoints. The two value sets and the weakest-input composition rule of observation_vantage and observation_directness are unchanged at 0.8.0, so those rows keep match_type exact. Coverage: records carrying a mapped field 0 to 16, and the evidence_vantage and verification_basis rows moved from inferred to emitted. Added: the revisions[].reason_code row against revision_reason (AVE added the array in #360, copying the four codes from this registry), a registry_term_uri on every row, and gaps for the 28 registry terms added since 0.2.0. Corrected: ave_evidence_fields_total was stated as 7 on 2026-09-15 while the fields the file mapped or listed as gaps were 8, and detection_methodology, also a schema property, was in neither list; it is now listed as a gap, and the total is 10 with revisions added.
